study type: Cohort study with longitudinal and cross-sectional analyses
outcome: Mode of delivery (unplanned cesarean section, planned cesarean section, vacuum extraction)
cohort: The study enrolled 3141 mothers and assessed their sleep at four time points during pregnancy and at delivery.
finding: Poor and short maternal sleep quality and duration during mid- and late pregnancy were associated with longer delivery duration and an increased likelihood of operative deliveries.
mod_finding: Poor sleep quality in late pregnancy and at delivery, as well as short sleep duration and frequent nocturnal awakenings, were associated with an increased risk of unplanned or planned cesarean section and vacuum extraction.
cross-section timing: Early pregnancy, mid-pregnancy, late pregnancy, and at delivery
